check: MISMATCH: the CD74 / HLA-DRB1 / TYROBP claims do not come from Norman (GSE133344, K562). Norman's 670 gene models never use CD74, HLA-DRB1 or TYROBP sequences and there is no CD74 response model in Norman. All four claims match GSE153056 (Papalexi 2021, THP-1 ECCITE-seq CRISPR knockout, 300 gene models, held-out replicate rep1): top CD74 sequence used by 111 models (claim 111, OK); top HLA-DRB1 sequence used by 66 models (claim 66, OK); top TYROBP sequence used by 185 models (claim 185, OK); HLA-DRB1 is the top feature of the CD74 model with share 0.26828 over 20 sequences (next SH3BGRL3 0.15043) (OK). CD74 model fit r = 0.9898 across 25 perturbations. Score 0.890 = Norman PerturBench seen-perturbation cosine of log fold change (BENCH.seen.Norman.p2g = 0.8904, 43 held-out doubles, 729 genes), so the score belongs to Norman while the CD74 example belongs to GSE153056; the card must name both studies or switch one. genes = Norman (matches the card label); genes_GSE153056 = same table for the study the CD74 example comes from. n_models = number of response-gene models using at least one sequence from that gene (page closeup 'nr'); max_models_one_sequence = largest count for a single sequence of that gene on the gene track (only the ~60 drawn genes). example_targets = response genes where that gene has the largest share. CD74 direction: per-model coefficients are only visible for up to 5 users per sequence, so direction = sign of summed visible coef of that gene's sequences in the CD74 model, with pos/neg counts; null where none visible. Data: live artifact 7n2eedbbXKyR6nfL3My9jv (version 1791491039-322a), P3 object + p3data/*.k.js. The other page (5n3dkFuoBT2tcmjDR6YLoP) holds only the known-perturbation Pearson delta tables; it has no per-gene sequence-use data.
